subject: science
intro: Mr. Patel here. Let's plan a lesson on why weather changes when air masses meet.

beats.narration: A dramatic title for a dramatic topic, since this is where storms come from.
This standard is about how the motion and interaction of air masses cause changes in weather.
Focused on cause and effect, since that's the core of this standard.
beats.text: Students will be able to explain how the interaction of warm and cold air masses at a front causes changes in weather conditions.

beats.narration: Using a local recent map makes it feel real.
beats.text: Show a weather map from last week with a cold front. "What do you predict happened to the weather here as the front passed?"

beats.narration: The tank demo makes something invisible visible.
beats.text: Demo with a divided tank of warm (red) and cold (blue) water: remove the divider and watch the cold water slide under. Connect to cold fronts lifting warm air, which cools and forms clouds.

beats.narration: Real data practice is what the standard actually asks for.
beats.text: Groups analyze three days of real weather data (temperature, pressure, wind, precipitation) and identify when a front passed, citing data.

beats.narration: The required words check the mechanism, not just the result.
beats.text: Explain what happens to the weather when a cold front passes, using the words "dense," "rises," and "condenses."

outro: Map, demo, real data. Your turn to plan.
